record.paper_title: Some open problems in dynamical systems
record.original_question: For a C^∞-generic Hamiltonian H, can one find a closed connected invariant set F ⊂ H^{-1}(1) that contains the supports of all ergodic minimizing measures, has the property that orbits asymptotic to locally minimizing orbits are dense in F, and also carries a dense orbit of the Hamiltonian flow itself?

evidence.quote: 4. Can one ﬁnd C∞ -generically a closed connected set F , invariant by the Hamiltonian ﬂow fH t of H, F⊂H−1(1), such that F contains all the supports of the ergodic minimal measures, in F the orbits asymptotic to the locally minimal orbits ... are dense in F , and on F , fH t|F has a dense orbit ?

artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a resolution of this generic existence question concerning a closed connected invariant set in a fixed energy level that simultaneously contains all supports of ergodic minimal measures, has the locally-minimizing asymptotic orbits dense in it, and carries a dense flow orbit. The problem is stated as an open question in surveys of open problems in dynamical systems related to Mather's variational theory and Arnold diffusion, and no published proof or counterexample appears in the search results.

status_evidence.title: The link between the shape of the Aubry-Mather sets and the minimizing measures
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses structure of Aubry-Mather sets and minimizing measures, without resolving the generic existence of a single invariant connected set carrying a dense orbit and containing all minimizing supports.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related literature treats Aubry-Mather sets but does not establish the conjectured generic invariant set.

status_evidence.title: Invariant measures of Hamiltonian systems with prescribed asymptotic Maslov index
status_evidence.snippet: Studies minimal ergodic invariant measures for Tonelli Hamiltonians via an analogue of Mather's beta function.
status_evidence.claim: Work on minimal measures continues but the generic-connected-invariant-set question remains unanswered in the literature found.
